# The Water-Stone of the Wise

But truly it is even more to be wondered at that some men are found who not only inquire into this highest art <note>original: *Ecclesiastes 7*</note> but even attempt to handle and practice it, and yet nevertheless doubt whether it be a natural and truly magical art, or instead a preternatural and necromantic one, which might be acquired only through spirits and unlawful, forbidden means. Not at all, my good man; the Devil and all the impious have no such power without divine permission that they might touch even the smallest part of this art, much less master it or exercise it according to their own pleasure. Not in the least, I say; that power resides in the hand and authority of God alone, who imparts it to whom He wills and, at the same time, takes it away again. For to this art, which takes its origin from and out of God, no seekers of pleasure are admitted, much less dire and infernal spirits; but rather, in their place, such a spirit as is simple, upright, true, constant, and of a pure and pious essence. Yet the modern world, in its careless impiety, does not recognize this spirit, and therefore remains ignorant of its essence and its supreme mystery in many respects. For as soon as it hears anything of this with its ears, and yet cannot quickly comprehend it, then these worldly companions <note>original: *Wisdom 1*</note> call it foolishness. Therefore also, because of their blindness, that spirit shall be perpetually hidden from them, and finally taken away from them altogether.

<note>A small ink flourish or doodle consisting of several wavy vertical and horizontal strokes appears in the right margin.</note>

Lest I wander perhaps further than is just from my purpose by this reminder, let me touch upon it again and finally bring it to a conclusion. Therefore, I wish this to be properly instilled into pious artists as a friendly exhortation: that to the extent a man directs his heart and mind—indeed, his very life and actions—toward God <note>original: *Ecclesiastes 18 & 29*</note>, to that same extent he shall perceive a remarkable benefit in the progress of the stone and of his labor, daily and even at every hour. This is what I myself have observed every day with the greatest diligence and great devotion, and thus I have experienced it by the very fact. For this reason, one ought to direct all his actions toward this from the very beginning, and so prepare himself that he may afterwards be able to achieve a more happy end in both works <note>referring to both the spiritual and the physical alchemical operations</note>.
